title: Protocol for multi-scale light microscopy/electron microscopy neuronal imaging in mouse brain tissue
protocol: Sacrifice mice injected with the AAV2/1-SynTetOff-EGFP-APEX2 vector by ip injection of overdose of Somnopentyl® (200 mg/kg).
Open the thoracic cavity with surgical scissors.
Make an incision to the right atrial appendage with surgical scissors.
Insert a 22-gauge needle into the left ventricle of heart.
Perfuse with 20 ml of ice-cold PBS using a 20 ml syringe.
Perfuse with 20 ml of the ice-cold fixative solution using another 20 ml syringe.
Excise brains using surgical scissors and tweezers.
Immerse the brain in the fixative solution and rock gently for 16 h–20 h at 4°C (50 rpm–100 rpm).
Embed the brain tissues in 4% agar in PBS in a standard 6-well culture plate.
Allow the agar to solidify on ice for 30 min.
Stick a piece of mending tape on the bottom of the specimen tray.
Attach the tray to the bath.
Trim the agar block with a razor blade to square off the sides.
Mount the agar block onto the tape with superglue.
Pour ice-cold 0.1 M PB into the specimen tray.
Set the sectioning speed to 0.14 mm/s with 1.4 mm amplitude.
Set the vibratome frequency to 75 Hz–77 Hz.
Cut 1-mm-thick brain slices.
Collect the slices in ice-cold PBS.
Store the slices in PBS for 16 h–20 h at 4°C if not used immediately.
Prepare a solution for APEX2/BT-GO reaction without NaN3 preservative.
Perform APEX2/BT-GO reaction in a standard 6-well culture plate at 20°C–25°C.
Immerse the slices in 10 mL of permeabilization buffer in a 13 mL centrifuge tube.
Rock gently for 4 h (50 rpm–100 rpm).
Transfer the slices in 8 mL of 0.1 M PB.
Wash the slices with 8 mL of 0.1 M PB three times, each for 5 min with gentle rocking (50 rpm–100 rpm).
Transfer the slices in 1200 μL of BT-GO reaction mixture in a 2 mL safe-lock microcentrifuge tube.
Rock gently for 4 h (50 rpm–100 rpm).
Add 12 μL of β-D-glucose solution to the BT-GO reaction mixture.
Rock gently for 2 h (50 rpm–100 rpm).
Transfer the slices in 8 mL of PBS.
Wash the slices with 8 mL of PBS for 15 minutes twice with gentle rocking.
Immerse the slices in 8 mL of 4% PFA in 0.1 M PB.
Rock gently for 16 hours to 20 hours at 4°C.
Transfer the slices in 8 mL of PBS.
Wash the slices with 8 mL of PBS for 5 minutes twice with gentle shaking.
Warm ScaleS0 and ScaleS4 solutions to 37°C.
Immerse the brain slices in 8 mL of ScaleS0 solution.
Rock gently for 2 hours at 37°C.
Transfer slices into 8 mL of 1× PBS and wash twice for 15 minutes each at 20°C-25°C with gentle rocking (50 rpm-100 rpm).
Transfer slices into 8 mL of ScaleS4 solution and rock gently for 8 hours to 12 hours at 37°C (90 rpm).
Place cleared brain slices on the bottom coverslip of the imaging chamber.
Remove excessive ScaleS4 solution around the cleared slice.
Drop ScaleS4 gel onto the cleared slice to fill the imaging chamber, maintaining a temperature of 37°C for the gel.
Mount a coverslip on the imaging chamber and place Kimwipe paper and a slide glass in this order on top of the coverslip.
Transfer the imaging chamber into a refrigerator at 4°C.
Place metal weights on the slide glass and allow the ScaleS4 gel to solidify for 30 minutes.
Remove metal weights, slide glass, Kimwipe paper, and coverslip from the imaging chamber, wiping away excess ScaleS4 gel.
Attach the imaging chamber to the bottom of a 60-mm glass petri dish with Blu-Tack® at multiple points.
Pour ScaleS4 solution into the dish and incubate the embedded slice in the solution for 60 minutes at 20°C-25°C with gentle agitation (40 rpm-60 rpm).
Substitute with fresh ScaleS4 solution to remove air bubbles from the sample surface.
Mount the imaging chamber on a microscope stage.
Immerse the objective lens in ScaleS4 solution, and make it approach to the cleared slice slowly.
Adjust imaging acquisition settings such as laser power, scan speed, pinhole diameter, detector gain, amplifier offset/gain, xy and z-axis resolution and bit intensity resolution.
Collect images by a CLSM, and record captured images.
Remove ScaleS4 gel around the imaged brain slices.
Immerse the slice in 8 mL of 1× PBS and wash twice for 15 min each with gentle rocking at 20°C–25°C.
Immerse the slices in 8 mL of 4% PFA in 0.1 M PB, and rock gently for 16 h–20 h at 4°C.
Transfer the slices into 8 mL of 1× PBS and wash twice with 8 mL of 1× PBS for 5 min each with gentle shaking.
Store the slices in 0.02% NaN3 in PBS at 4°C for up to 1 week.
Immerse the slices in 8 mL of 30% sucrose in 0.1 M PB until they sink completely.
Place the slice in a cryomold containing OCT compound after immersing it in OCT compound for 15 min.
Cool isopentane almost to its freezing temperature by placing it in a metal container on liquid nitrogen.
Immerse the cryomold into the cooled isopentane to freeze and then transfer it into a freezer at −20°C.
Store the blocks in a freezer at −20°C for up to 1 week.
Mount the block onto the stage of a freezing microtome with OCT compound.
Quickly freeze the OCT compound using dry ice powder.
Leave the block in place for 5 min.
Cut the slice into 40-μm-thick sections.
Collect the sections in ice-cold 0.1 M PB.
Place a re-section on a slide with a brush.
Apply 75% glycerol in PBS to the re-section.
Lower a coverslip onto 75% glycerol in PBS to avoid trapping air bubbles.
Mount the slide on a microscope stage.
Adjust imaging acquisition settings such as laser power, scan speed, pinhole diameter, detector gain, amplifier offset/gain, xy and z-axis resolution and bit intensity resolution.
Collect images by a CLSM equipped with high NA objective lenses.
Record captured images.
Remove the coverslip from the slide.
Immerse the re-section in 8 mL of PBS in a standard 6-well culture plate.
Wash twice for 15 min with gentle rocking at 20°C–25°C (40 rpm–60 rpm).
Wash the sections in 3 mL of PBS and wash twice for 10 min with gentle rocking (50 rpm–100 rpm).
Immerse the sections in 500 μL of ABC solution in a standard 24-well plate, rock gently for 24 h (50 rpm–100 rpm).
Wash the sections in 3 mL of PBS and wash twice for 10 min with gentle rocking (50 rpm–100 rpm).
Immerse the sections in 1 mL of DAB-Ni2+ solution in a standard 24-well plate on ice, incubate for 10 min on ice with gentle agitation (40 rpm–60 rpm).
Add 3 μL of 0.1% H2O2 into DAB-Ni2+ solution and incubate on ice with gentle agitation until color development.
Immerse the sections in 3 mL of 2% NaN3 in PBS, incubate for 15 min at 20°C–25°C with gentle agitation (40 rpm–60 rpm).
Wash the sections in 3 mL of PBS at 4°C and wash twice for 10 min with gentle rocking (50 rpm–100 rpm).
Wash tissue sections in 3 mL of 0.1 M PB for 10 min twice.
Immerse the sections in 1 mL of 1% OsO4 in 0.1 M PB and incubate for 2 h in dark.
Wash the sections in 3 mL of 0.1 M PB for 10 min three times.
Wash the sections in 10 mL of ddH2O five times for 2 min with gentle rocking (50 rpm-100 rpm).
Immerse the sections in 1 mL of 2% UA in 50% EtOH and incubate for 30 min in dark.
Incubate the sections in ethanol solutions at increasing concentrations for 20 min each: 50%, 70%, 90%, 99.5%, 99.5%, 100%, and 100%.
Incubate the sections in propylene oxide for 20 min twice.
Immerse the sections in Epoxy resin/propylene oxide mixture and incubate for 1 h.
Immerse the sections in Epoxy resin and incubate for 16 h-20 h.
Place the sections onto silicone-coated slide glass and mount a silicone-coated coverslip on the slide.
Place metal weights on the coverslip to make the sections flat.
Polymerize the resin by heating in an oven at 60°C for 2 days.
Remove the coverslip from the slide with a razor blade.
Identify the region of interest (ROI) with a brightfield microscope.
Trim the ROI using a razor blade under a stereo microscope.
Mount the trimmed resin block on a flat-tipped rocket of the resin with glue.
Trim away excess resin with a razor blade.
Mount the rocket on the stage of an ultramicrotome, and align the block face with a synthetic diamond knife.
Remove the empty resin from the top of the sample using the synthetic diamond knife to expose the surface of the tissue.
Make ultrathin sections (60–80-nm thickness) with a diamond knife.
Collect short ribbons of ultrathin sections on TEM grids of copper, and let them dry.
Drop 1% UA solution on Parafilm®.
Place the grids on the droplet of 1% UA solution for 20 min.
Wash the grids three times by dipping them into 10 mL of ddH2O.
Place the grids on the droplet of lead citrate solution on Parafilm® for 2 min.
Wash the grids three times by dipping into 10 mL of ddH2O, and let them dry.
Set an accelerating voltage of 80 kV.
Set a filament voltage of approximately 20 V.
Load grids onto the grid holder.
Locate the region of interest under lower magnification mode.
Increase the magnification.
Acquire individual images.
Record captured images.
